title: Classification of Non-Hermitian Flat Bands
abstract: Exact flat bands provide a versatile setting for correlated and topological phenomena, yet their properties are controlled not only by their dispersion but also by the structure of their Bloch projectors. Here, we establish a projector-based classification of non-Hermitian flat bands. In contrast to Hermitian flat bands, non-Hermiticity introduces a biorthogonal projector whose left-right pairing permits a distinct norm-pole singularity. We identify four classes: analytic NH-A, continuous but nonanalytic NH-C, bounded but discontinuous NH-D, and pole-singular NH-E. We show that continuity of the biorthogonal projector preserves the locking of the right, left, and biorthogonal Chern numbers, $C_R=C_L=C_{\rm bi}$, thereby realizing non-Hermitian critical topological flat bands. Once continuity is lost, this locking can break down; in particular, a mismatch $C_R\neq C_L$ can occur in the NH-E class. Finally, we show that this Chern number mismatch ensures to produce an anomalous enhancement of resonant cross-orbital transfer. Our results establish biorthogonal projector regularity as the organizing principle linking compact localized states, topology, and driven response in non-Hermitian flat bands.
summary:
This paper introduces a comprehensive, projector-based classification system for non-Hermitian flat bands, distinguishing four classes based on the mathematical regularity of the system's biorthogonal projector. The core finding is that the breakdown of projector continuity leads to topological invariants mismatch ($C_R 
eq C_L$), which is directly correlated with an anomalous enhancement in resonant cross-orbital energy transfer.
main_problem: The paper establishes a projector-based classification scheme for non-Hermitian (NH) flat bands, extending known concepts from Hermitian systems.
main_result:
The classification identifies four classes (NH-A, NH-C, NH-D, NH-E) based on the regularity of the biorthogonal projector, showing that topological mismatch ($C_R 
eq C_L$) in the NH-E class leads to anomalous resonant cross-orbital transfer.
method: The methodology involves analyzing the mathematical regularity (analyticity, continuity, singularity) of the biorthogonal projector $P_{bi}(k)$ across the Brillouin zone and relating this regularity to topological invariants (Chern numbers) and transport properties.
model_or_system:
The study focuses on electronic systems exhibiting flat bands described by non-Hermitian Hamiltonians ($H 
eq H^\dagger$). The analysis compares the behavior of these bands across different mathematical regimes defined by the projector's properties.
key_observables: Right Chern number ($C_R$), Left Chern number ($C_L$), Biorthogonal Chern number ($C_{bi}$), and the cross-orbital transfer intensity $T_{B	o A}(k)$.
important_parameters: The classification depends critically on the regularity of the biorthogonal projector $P_{bi}(k)$ at the band touching points.
main_assumptions: The analysis is primarily restricted to rank-one flat bands, though generalizations to higher-rank manifolds are mentioned as future work.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between Hermitian and non-Hermitian classifications, showing band structures, projector magnitudes, and the scaling of maximum cross-orbital transfer intensity ($T_{	ext{max}}$) versus damping rate ($\eta$) for different classes.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the need for a projector-based classification for NH flat bands. It then details the four classes (NH-A to NH-E) based on projector regularity, linking each class to specific topological invariants and measurable physical responses like cross-orbital transfer scaling.
why_interesting: The work provides a rigorous mathematical framework linking topological invariants (Chern numbers) to measurable transport phenomena (cross-orbital transfer) in non-Hermitian systems, which is highly relevant for understanding open quantum systems and engineered materials.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Projector-regularity classification of Hermitian and non-Hermitian exact flat bands. (a) Hermitian flat bands are classified by the regularity of the flat-band projector PFB(k): analytic (H-A), continuous but nonanalytic (H-C), and discontinuous (H-D). In non-Hermitian systems, the corresponding classification is governed by the biorthogonal projector Pbi(k), yielding NH-A, NH-C, NH-D, and NH-E. (b) Relation to spectral isolation. A gapped flat band is necessarily analytic (H-A or NH-A), whereas gapless flat bands can realize all Hermitian classes or the NH-A–NH-E hierarchy, depending on the regularity of the corresponding projector.
